historical_references.reference: Sarvar ibn Mansur, a Persian Sultan of the Ilkhanate dynasty in the 13th century. He ruled from 1287 to 1291 AD.
historical_references.context: Sarvar is known for his military campaigns against the Mongols and his religious tolerance. He was a patron of Rumi and other Sufi poets and scholars.

historical_references.reference: Sarvar Mir Akbar, a Mughal emperor who ruled from 1560 to 1572 AD. He was the eldest son of Emperor Humayun and Haji Begum.
historical_references.context: Sarvar Mir Akbar was a capable military leader and expanded the Mughal empire. He was also a lover of arts and sciences and built many beautiful structures, including the Jami Masjid in Lahore.
